summary: Windows + PowerShell production-readiness review focused on repository structure, cleanliness, navigability, generated outputs, naming, duplicate assets, dead references, oversized files, and mixed responsibilities.
active_objective: Make the repository structure clean and navigable for a new production-ready Windows desktop project without introducing legacy folders, compatibility fallbacks, or historical tracker notes.
assumptions: Expected structure is the documented WPF/WebView2 desktop shell, React/Vite frontend, in-process .NET backend, Core contracts, Infrastructure adapters, Worker job abstractions, tests, PowerShell scripts, docs, packaging, and brand assets.
Only PROJECT_STATUS.json may be changed during this review.
current_tasks: Remove local generated outputs from the working tree before release handoff: artifacts, all bin and obj folders, src\OnlyRag.Web\dist, src\OnlyRag.Web\node_modules, src\OnlyRag.Web\tsconfig.tsbuildinfo, and packaging\qdrant\payload.
Remove the empty local directory src\components because it is outside the documented src\OnlyRag.* project layout and has no tracked responsibility.
Review duplicated tracked brand/web/GitHub assets and document or enforce a single source-of-truth generation path for copied PNG/SVG assets.

Split oversized production source files where responsibilities are mixed, starting with OCR provisioning, document controller state, settings actions, OCR engine process handling, app composition, retrieval ranking, settings endpoints, translation export, local document library, Ollama client, Office extraction, and SQLite migration.
Split oversized test files by scenario or fixture responsibility so production behavior remains navigable and failures are localized.
Review naming for broad controller/action/helper files and replace ambiguous responsibilities with feature-specific names during split work.
next_tasks: Run git status --short --ignored after cleanup to confirm only intentional ignored directories remain absent from the workspace.
Run markdown link validation again after structural cleanup.
Run the repository gate only after structure cleanup is complete.
blockers: The local workspace is not structurally clean because ignored generated outputs and an empty out-of-layout src\components directory are present.
Several production files exceed review thresholds and should be split before calling the repository production-ready for a new project handoff.
risks: Generated/local output size inspected under artifacts, src\OnlyRag.Web\dist, and packaging\qdrant\payload is about 442 MB across 615 files, increasing cleanup and handoff risk even though ignored.
Tracked asset duplicates exist across assets\brand, src\OnlyRag.Web\public, and .github\assets; without a clear source-of-truth rule, brand/public assets can drift.
Large UI controller and service files concentrate state, side effects, formatting, process orchestration, and API workflow logic, reducing navigability for production maintenance.
Large test files make scenario ownership harder to scan and can hide fixture duplication.
structure_notes: No broken local Markdown links were found in tracked Markdown files during this review.
No tracked old, backup, temp, misc, stuff, final, or new catch-all folders were found.
.gitignore covers the generated outputs observed in git status --short --ignored.
The tracked top-level layout is coherent, but local ignored outputs and the empty src\components directory reduce repository cleanliness and navigability.
handoff_notes: Keep this tracker limited to current structural cleanup and navigability work. Do not add historical completion notes.
